runs.text: We cannot understand the Everlasting Gospel until we first see one forgotten truth. This truth is: every human being is born with a nature inclined toward selfishness and sin. Through Adam’s sin, condemnation and the sentence of death passed to the entire human race. Every descendant of Adam enters the world spiritually dead, under condemnation—because all have sinned. “
If we claim to be without sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.” (1 John 1:8)

The doctrine of man’s character bent toward himself (selfishness) is one of the most important doctrines in the study of the Everlasting Gospel. It is against this backdrop that the gospel is presented. When the gospel is presented with this understanding intact, the sinner sees their need for a Savior, and then has a desire to exercise the faith needed to have a change in their sinful and selfish character.

When the gospel is presented with this aspect missing, the gospel often becomes the forgiveness of sin alone. When we have forgiveness alone without dealing with man’s broken character, we inevitably end up with a Christian church that has lost its ability to show the righteous life of Christ to the world. Even in Luther’s day, some perverted his message of justification by faith alone into (anti-law license) — a heresy Luther himself fiercely opposed and stood against by coining a new Latin word, “antinomianism”, or (anti-law).

The misunderstanding of the nature of man is not an error of antinomianism alone. It also leads many into legalism. There are aspects of legalism that are more subtle than many suspect. Many who have come to Christ by faith alone, then imagine themselves as having the ability to change their own sinful nature. They give lip service to faith by using Christ’s name, but in reality their lives only show evidence of self-righteousness, and the absence of genuine love.

Our fallen condition penetrates to the very core of our being. The Bible teaches that, as a result of the fall of man, (Genesis 3:6) every part of man’s nature has been corrupted by sin. The Bible uses the phrase, “the flesh” to describe the sinful nature of man, bent toward himself.
Those who cannot see their own inner corruption are often self-righteous. Self-righteousness never looks good on a human. Self-righteousness is often demonstrated in the most horrendous acts of evil.
MAN’S UN-RIGHTEOUSNESS:
1. How does the Bible describe man’s righteousness?
Isaiah 64:6
But we are all as an unclean thing, and
all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags.
Note:

Many Christians have been reading this text for decades assuming that it means that all of our unrighteousness is as filthy rags. But man’s sin problem runs much deeper than many have imagined. In fact, this text shows that every act of self-produced righteousness is polluted and unacceptable to God.
All
of our righteousnesses are indeed as filthy rags!
2. Does Jesus say that a corrupt tree can produce good fruit?
Matthew 7:18
A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit,
neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit
Note:
Jesus states that a corrupt tree cannot bring forth good fruit! We need God’s power from above.
3. Can a natural person see their own corruption?
Jeremiah 17:9
The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it
Note:
The depravity of man is seen throughout the Bible. Man’s heart is “deceitful and desperately wicked.”
4. What does the Bible say that men love?
John 3:19
And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and
men loved darkness rather than light,
because their deeds were evil.
Note:
Not only are men unrighteous, but they love darkness. We do this because light reveals that our deeds are evil.
LAODICEA:
5. What type of witness is Christ to the churches?
Revelation 3:14
And unto the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write;
These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness
Note:

Laodicea is the last church in the list of seven churches in the book of Revelation. Many Bible scholars see the seven churches as seven time periods in the Christian era, and conclude that Laodicea is an allegory of the last church before the return of Christ.

God says that Laodicea is poor, wretched, and miserable. Laodicea sees herself as rich and increased, in need of nothing. Who is telling the truth? This is why Christ addresses Laodicea as the “True Witness.”
6. What type of works should Laodicea have?
Revelation 3:15
I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot
. 16 So then
because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.
Note:
Jesus says he wishes Laodicea had either hot or cold works. But because Laodicea has lukewarm works He will spew her out of His mouth.
Hot works
= zealous works of faith. (Gal. 5:6)
Cold works
= legalistic works of the law. (Gal. 3:2,3)
Lukewarm works
= a mixture of both. (Rev. 3:15,16)
Jesus wants us HOT—fully on fire for Him, filled with His love and righteousness, not mingled with lukewarm self-righteous works. He wants works of faith, reflecting His love dwelling in our hearts.
7. How does the True Witness respond to Laodicea?
Revelation 3:17
Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked.
Note:
Christ is the True Witness. (See Revelation 3:14) Laodicea’s works make her wretched, miserable, poor, blind, and naked. What makes her destitute are her own intermingled self-righteous works.
8. What does Christ ask Laodicea to buy?
Revelation 3:18
I counsel thee to

buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eye-salve, that thou mayest see
Gold tried in the fire
= Pure faith that works by love and purifies the heart. (See 1 Peter 1:7,8)
White raiment
= The spotless righteousness of Christ to cover our spiritual nakedness. (See Rev 7:13-14)
Eye-salve
= The anointing of the Holy Spirit that opens our eyes to see our true condition. (Rev. 3:18)
Note:

These are the very things Laodicea lacks, yet proudly thinks she does not need. The lack of Gold tried in the fire and white raiment are symptoms of her self-righteousness. She needs eye-salve to show her that she is lacking the faith that produces Christ’s love.
9. What good works should Christians have?
John 14:12
He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also
and greater works than these shall he do
; because I go unto my Father.
Note:

Christ expects us to do the impossible. We must have the works of Christ. It may sound impossible to do greater world than Christ’s, but these works can be ours because Christ goes unto His Father. He will then send His Spirit to produce good fruit in our lives.
Galatians 5:22
The fruit of the Spirit is
: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.
10. How does God want Laodicea to respond to His loving chastisement?
Revelation 3:19
As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten:
be zealous therefore, and repent
Note:

Laodicea is not repentant! She takes pride in her own spiritual attainments. Even when taught a new fact about the Bible, she will often exclaim, “I already knew all this!” In her pride she thinks she knows all!

“The message to the Laodicean church is applicable to our condition. How plainly is pictured the position of those who think they have all the truth, who take pride in their knowledge of the Word of God, while its sanctifying power has not been felt in their lives. The fervor of the love of God is wanting in their hearts, but it is this very fervor of love that makes God's people the light of the world.”
11. How should Laodicea respond to His voice?
Revelation 3:20
Behold, I stand at the door, and knock:
if any man hear my voice,
and open the door
I will come in to him.
Note:

“While those addressed are flattering them-selves that they are in an exalted spiritual condition, the message of the True Witness breaks their security by the startling denunciation of their true condition of spiritual blindness, poverty, and wretchedness. The testimony, so cutting and severe, cannot be a mistake, for it is the True Witness who speaks, and His testimony must be correct.”

When we finally look at our selfishness and surrender it to God, when the whole heart is given to Him, then our heart’s door is opened. It is not a spasmodic here-and-there effort, but a lifelong love. Our intermingled self-righteous pride and efforts will then cease, we will turn our faces toward Him with love and humility, and then our open heart will beat in harmony with His will.
FOOLISH VIRGINS:
12. How many slept while awaiting the bridegroom?
Matthew 25:1
Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins,

which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom. 2 And five of them were wise, and five were foolish. 3 They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: 4 But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. 5
While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept
Note:
Notice the similarities between the ten virgins and Laodicea. Both groups are awaiting the kingdom of God. Both groups are at the end of time, and both groups must overcome.
13. What happened to the door for the foolish virgins?
Matthew 25:8
And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.
But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves
And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage:
and the door was shut
Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us.
But he answered and said, “Verily I say unto you,
I know you not
Note:

The messages to both Laodicea, and the foolish virgins are associated with a door. Christ knocks at Laodicea's door seeking entry, (See Revelation 3:20) and finally for the foolish virgins, the door is shut. (See Matthew 25:10) To open the door means we are finally willing to look at our own deformity. “Not to see our own deformity is not to see the beauty of Christ’s character.” “He who does not abhor (detest) himself cannot understand the meaning of redemption.”
DON’T BECOME DISCOURAGED WITH SELF AS YOU BEHOLD CHRIST’S PERFECTION:
14. How did the righteous answer Jesus?
Matthew 25:37
Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink
Note:

By walking in the Spirit, (Eph. 2:10) the redeemed have fed the hungry, they have clothed the naked, and visited the prisoners. They have done the works of Christ because He has gone to the Father and they believe in Him. (See John 14:12) But after arriving in Heaven, when Jesus points out these good works, they do not recognize them as their own! When a true Christian compares themselves to Christ, they will always appear sinful in their own eyes.
After seeing the beauty of Christ’s character, we lose our own self-righteousness. In effect, we obtain the
Eye-salve
to see our true condition. We then abhor self, sense our desperate need, and buy from Him…
White raiment
In humility we obtain His perfect robe.
G
old tried in fire
We behold His self-sacrificing love, and respond with a faith that works by love.
The closer we come to Jesus, the more faulty we now appear in our own eyes.
” This is evidence that the self-righteous delusions from Satan have lost their power; and we can come to Jesus with our great need.
15. How can we serve the law of God?
Romans 7:25
So then with the mind I myself serve the law of God; but with the flesh the law of sin.
Note:

When a person comes to Christ, they receive a new mind that desires the things of God. But at the same time they enter into a lifelong warfare with the corrupt desires of their own flesh. So, what part do we play in obtaining true victory?
Victory comes only through the negative first!
Negative:
We die, we crucify the flesh with its lusts, and we mortify its deeds. (Galatians 5:24) It is
through the Spirit
that we mortify the flesh! (Romans 8:13)
Positive:
Then Christ’s positive life and fruit flows in us as we walk in His Spirit.
Galatians 5:22
The fruit of the Spirit is
: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.
This fruit fulfills the law’s righteous requirements in our hearts. (See Galatians 5:16, 23; Romans 8:4)

The reason that our part is in the negative is because we have no positive good works to offer. Our own righteous deeds are as filthy rags. Our only hope is to be crucified with Christ, so He can then live in us and produce positive fruit. (See Gal. 2:20; 5:22, 23)
“It will then be as natural for us to minister to the needy and suffering as it was for Christ to go about doing good.” (See Isaiah 58:6-7; Matthew 25:35-40)
16. What does the Bible say dwells in the flesh?
Romans 7:18
For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing
: for to will is present with me;
but how to perform that which is good I find not
Note:

Even Apostle Paul struggled against his flesh. Romans chapter 7 pictures the struggle of one who tries to obey God’s law in the strength of his own flesh. The cry, “O wretched man that I am!” is answered immediately in Romans chapter 8.
Romans 8:3
For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh
That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.
Note:
When we walk in Christ, the tendencies of our fallen nature are subdued and brought under His control. “
I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but
Christ liveth in me
”. (Gal. 2:20) By daily dying to self and allowing Jesus to reign, the believer’s character ultimately reflects Christ’s character.
17. Who delivers Paul from his body of death?
Romans 7:24
O wretched man that I am! who shall deliver me from the body of this death
I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Note:
Paul detested his fallen flesh. Does Paul find victory? “Yes!” He thanks God that he has found victory through Christ.
18. How do we get victory over the flesh?
Ephesians 3:20
Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think,
according to the power that worketh in us
Note:
Christ’s Spirit dwelling in us gives us power to crucify our sinful nature. (See also
Romans. 8:13
19. Whose workmanship produces our good works?
Ephesians 2:10
For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them.
” (NKJV)
Note:
Good works flow out of us as naturally as fruit from a healthy vine. Christ’s true works were there
beforehand
. We need to walk in these works today!
John 15:4, 5
Abide in Me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in Me. I am the vine, you are the branches.
He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing.
20. Will the saints gain victory over their flesh?
Philippians 1:6
Being confident of this very thing, that
he which hath begun a good work in you will
perform it
until the day of Jesus Christ
Note:

Yes! “When self is merged in Christ, love springs forth spontaneously. The completeness of Christian character is attained when the impulse to help and bless others springs constantly from within, when the sunshine of heaven fills the heart and is revealed in the countenance.”
“He will accomplish this in all who do not interpose a perverse will and thus frustrate his grace”.
It is Christ who does the performing! See the end of the above sentence in verse 6 - (
He-
will perform it
“GENUINE LOVE” = (GOLD TRIED BY FIRE)
21. Where does genuine, true love come from?
1John 4:10
Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins
Note:
Laodicea boasts of her own wonderful works. She even boasts that she keeps the Ten Commandments because she “loves God!”
But is something missing
Yes,
g
old tried in the fire is missing.
She is missing faith that works by love. She is blind to her own lack of true love and in her pride she cannot see that she does not truly know Jesus. (See Matthew 25:11,12)
We cannot have genuine love until we first see some-thing. We must first behold God’s love for us.
Many boast of their love for God, but if they could see the contrast between their own selfish love and His perfect love they would never make such a boast! Seeing this contrast is the
eye-salve
that opens our eyes to reveal that our own love has been centered in ourselves.
BY BEHOLDING WE BECOME CHANGED:
Jesus is knocking at the door of our hearts. It is up to us to open the door.
We truly open it when we discover that all good works are His works
(Ephesians 2:10)
and that fallen humanity can love God only by beholding His true love for us.
(See 1 John 4:10, 19)

When Laodicea beholds Christ’s perfect selfless love, she will abhor her own lukewarm, self-righteous state. Failure to see a contrast between Christ’s love and our love, cheapens God’s love, and brings it down to our level. But seeing God’s true love enables us to finally love others genuinely, which is the
gold refined by fire.
When Laodicea finally has Christ’s authentic love and good works,
she will
not
be able to see these works in herself.
God sees her fruit clearly, but as she beholds His beauty, she abhors her own condition.

This is the vital contrast that finally awakens Laodicea. Those who have compared their own self-love to His pure love will not boast of an exalted spiritual condition. They have beheld Christ’s love, and therefore, can now see themselves as they truly are: wretched, miserable, blind, and naked. In seeing this contrast they finally sense their desperate need of Him.
